## Round 2 (2026-10-21)

Sources are spe/predictions/r02.yaml, saved before the run, and spe/evals/results/r02/r02.json. Each cell ran 5 trials on 40 tickets, so each cell has 200 graded tickets.

The r02 prediction did not name a grader field for "pass rate". This log reads it as `category_acc`. The prediction also gave no tolerance. This log counts a pass rate as a Hit when it lands within 0.02 of the prediction. It counts a cost as a Hit when it lands within 25 percent. Both rules are close-out defaults, logged in disagreements.md.

| Metric | Config | Predicted | Measured | Same as last round | Verdict | Closer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| category_acc | A | 0.85 | 0.86 | 0.84 | Hit (+0.01) | Prediction |
| category_acc | B | 0.88 | 0.86 | 0.84 | Hit (-0.02), Why broke | Tie |
| category_acc | C | 0.90 | 0.80 | 0.84 | Miss (-0.10) | Naive |
| category_acc | D | 0.75 | 0.74 | 0.70 | Hit (-0.01) | Prediction |
| priority_acc | C | 0.80 | 0.71 | none recorded | Miss (-0.09) | n/a |
| cost_per_ticket | D | $0.002 | $0.004 | none recorded | Miss (2x) | n/a |

- Mean absolute error on pass rate was 0.035 for the predictions and 0.030 for the same-as-last-round guess.
- The naive guess beat the predictions on mean error. The C miss of 0.10 caused this.
- The predictions hit 3 of 4 pass rates within 0.02. The naive guess hit 2 of 4.
- Both secondary predictions missed. These were C priority and D cost.
- Some results had no prediction. B cut cost from $0.011 to $0.009 per ticket at the same accuracy as A. C cut tool calls from 4.1 to 2.6. No one predicted tool calls.

### Which Why broke

- **B, "shorter prompt keeps focus."** B scored 0.86, the same as A. The number landed inside the tolerance, but the predicted 0.03 gain over A did not appear. The wrong assumption was that A lost accuracy because its prompt was long. It did not. The shorter prompt only lowered cost.
- **C, "merged tools cut wrong tool choice."** C made fewer calls (2.6 against 4.1). C also never called check_status on 9 outage tickets (trials r02-C-T17-1..3). The wrong assumption was that fewer tools lead to better tool choice. Merging the tools hid a call the model needed. The priority drop to 0.71 probably comes from those skipped calls, because outage priority depends on status. r02.json has no breakdown by ticket type, so this link is not confirmed.
- **D, "same design on a smaller model loses about 0.15."** The pass rate hit (0.74 against 0.75). The yaml does not say which config D copies. D made 3.9 tool calls, which matches A and B and not C. Measured against A, D lost 0.12. If D copies C instead, the number hit only because two errors cancelled. C was 0.10 below its prediction, and the real gap from C to D was 0.06, not 0.15. The cost number had no Why. The $0.002 figure assumed no retries. D retried on tickets over 2,000 words, and those retries doubled its tokens.

## F8. A merged tool hides a call the agent needs

- **Kind:** agent design, tool surface
- **Round:** r02
- **What:** Config C merged the lookup tools into fewer tools. C then never called check_status on 9 outage tickets. Its category_acc fell to 0.80 and its priority_acc fell to 0.71. Config A scored 0.86 and 0.79.
- **How to spot it:** Count check_status calls on outage tickets for each trial. Any outage ticket with no check_status call is this failure. Also compare tool_calls per ticket with A. A large drop together with lower accuracy points here.
- **Seen in:** r02-C-T17-1, r02-C-T17-2, r02-C-T17-3
- **Fix:** Split check_status back out of the merged tool, or make the merged tool always return status for outage tickets. Add a grader check for the check_status call rate on outage tickets. Report results by ticket type so outage tickets show up as their own row.

## F9. Retries on long tickets double the cost

- **Kind:** cost, agent behavior
- **Round:** r02
- **What:** Config D retried on tickets over 2,000 words. Each retry doubled the tokens for that ticket. D cost $0.004 per ticket against a prediction of $0.002.
- **How to spot it:** Group tokens per ticket by ticket length. If tickets over 2,000 words use about twice the tokens of one clean pass, retries are the cause. Also count retry events per trial.
- **Seen in:** r02 D, all trials with tickets over 2,000 words (r02.json notes)
- **Fix:** Turn off the retry or cap it for long tickets, and measure the accuracy cost of doing so. Report tokens and cost by ticket length. Price retries into the cost prediction.
